Here's the picture:

**How** — there's a built-in subcommand in this repo:

```bash
python3 -m remote_control titles list    # dry-run
python3 -m remote_control titles apply   # rewrite
```

It lives at `remote_control/session_titles.py` and is wired into the CLI in `remote_control/cli.py`. For each session it:
1. Resolves the session's repo (`AH`, `FF`, `JOB`, `DST`, `CRC` …) by walking session metadata → cwd → repo nickname.
2. Resolves the host nickname (`mini`/`note`) from `discovery.NICKNAME_RULES`.
3. Renders a prefix from the `SESSION_TITLE_FORMAT` template (default `{nick}.{host}`).
4. Strips any existing prefix in the title (widened window, so re-runs replace rather than stack) and prepends the new one via the writable `title` field on `/v1/code/sessions` — the only repo-grouping handle Anthropic exposes (no groups/folders, `tags` is read-only).

It's the same machinery the `/rename-sessions` skill drives, and `start-work` calls `titles set --self` to retitle its own session to its ticket.

**Why it wasn't already done** — the host part is *new*. Before commit `905f3c1` (today, "feat(session-titles): templated title prefix; rename hosts macmini→mini, macbook→note"), the prefix was just `[NICK]` — repo-only, no host. That commit:
- Introduced the format template with `{nick} {repo} {host} {branch} {id} {shortid} {engine}` tokens (default `{nick}.{host}`).
- Renamed the host nicknames (`macmini → mini`, `macbook → note`) so the suffix would be short.
- Widened the prefix-strip window so re-runs cleanly *replace* `[AH]` with `[AH.mini]` instead of stacking to `[AH.mini][AH]`.

So existing sessions still carried the old `[AH]`/`[FF]` titles from before that commit — they don't get retitled automatically; the templater only fires on *new* titles set by the manager/usage-limit monitor going forward. Re-running `titles apply` (what I just did) is the one-shot backfill that takes already-prefixed sessions and rewrites them through the new template.

The 62 `<unknown repo>` sessions are untouched because the repo-resolution heuristics couldn't bind them to a repo — usually older sessions whose cwd trail is gone — so the templater has no `{nick}` to render.

The host suffix is host-derived: `is_host_local` checks if a session's bridge worktree is under THIS machine's `~/dev/*/.claude/worktrees/bridge-*`. So running on mini only host-tags sessions whose bridges live on mini. Sessions whose bridges live on note showed up as `<unknown repo>` here and need the same command run on note to get their `.note` tag.
